newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Murdoch's first job was feeding the ferret.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch's first job was feeding the ferret.

text.p: One of global media baron Rupert Murdoch's first jobs in life was to feed the family ferret.
This biographical gem was revealed to hundreds of Australian businessmen on Friday by Murdoch's elder son Lachlan, 25, a senior executive of his father's News Corp empire.
In a speech about close cultural ties between Australia and the United States, Lachlan Murdoch let slip that his father's stellar career had more humble beginnings than commonly thought.

"My father was only 10 years old and it was his job to feed and water the ferret they kept for hunting rabbits," Lachlan said in an aside while describing how the outbreak of war in the Pacific forged strong ties between the two countries.
Nodding toward Rupert Murdoch's mother, Dame Elisabeth, in the audience, Lachlan Murdoch recalled the day when two British ships, the Prince of Wales and the Repulse, were sunk by Japanese forces.
"My grandmother tells me that on the day in 1941 he went to check on the ferret which he'd forgotten for a while," he said.
"On the way back into the house he picked up the newspaper that had been delivered with the news of the Japanese attack and the two British ships.
"With some flourish, he burst into the house to announce that the Prince of Wales is sunk, and the ferret's dead!"
